q1: Decision: if treatment must start before the liquid biopsy returns, begin empirical single-agent chemotherapy - oral temozolomide is the reasonable choice - while explicitly keeping the diagnostic work-up open; anthracycline-based soft-tissue-sarcoma regimens are the reserved next class, and a clinical trial is preferred whenever accessible. Key reasons: (1) the histologic entity is still not established (2026-11-04 surgical pathology: 'high-grade spindle cell/mesenchymal neoplasm, NOS'; STAT6 negative; no NAB2-STAT6 fusion), so no evidence-based standard regimen exists and any chemotherapy is by definition empirical - it must be paired with an agreed response checkpoint (repeat brain and whole-spine MRI after about 2-3 cycles / 8-12 weeks against the 2026-12-12 baseline) rather than being continued indefinitely; (2) temozolomide fits this situation best: oral, no vascular access needed, penetrates the CNS, reported activity in high-grade/mesenchymal CNS tumours (for example gliosarcoma-type lesions) and modest activity in several soft-tissue sarcomas, usually well tolerated at ECOG 1, and light enough on myelosuppression to preserve marrow reserve for later lines - typically 150-200 mg/m2 on days 1-5 of a 28-day cycle (or metronomic 75 mg/m2 daily) with CBC before each cycle, TMP-SMX if lymphopenic on prolonged dosing, and attention to mood, nausea and cytopenias; (3) if pathology ultimately resolves toward an extracranial-type soft-tissue sarcoma - the leading family for a high-grade spindle-cell mesenchymal tumour - the standard systemic backbone is anthracycline-based (doxorubicin, doxorubicin plus ifosfamide, or gemcitabine/docetaxel, with dacarbazine as an alternative), so before committing to any anthracycline obtain baseline echocardiography and complete the fertility-preservation and hepatitis-B/CBC work-up now, to keep that option real; (4) platinum/etoposide-type regimens belong to a carcinoma-like or small-round-cell differential and should not be used empirically while the entity is undefined; (5) chemotherapy answers neither local control nor diagnosis: the growing left frontal residual adjacent to eloquent cortex remains a re-operation and stereotactic-radiosurgery question for the tumour board (the bed has already had 60 Gy in 30 fractions), the stable C6 pial nodule is followed on imaging, and intrathecal chemotherapy is not indicated without confirmed leptomeningeal disease; (6) continue the parallel diagnostic pathway - methylation profiling plus DNA/RNA NGS on the archival blocks, and completion of systemic staging - because the result, not the calendar, should decide the next line.
q2: Decision: no - do not add a second chemotherapy drug now. Continue single-agent temozolomide to an adequate trial (about 2-3 cycles / 8-12 weeks) with the agreed MRI reassessment, and use the interval to secure the molecular diagnosis rather than to escalate toxicity. Key reasons: (1) the entity is still unclassified ('high-grade spindle cell/mesenchymal neoplasm, NOS', STAT6 negative, NAB2-STAT6 not detected), so no evidence base exists for any temozolomide combination in this patient - the published combinations (TMZ with bevacizumab, nitrosourea/procarbazine-type regimens, platinum or etoposide, or gemcitabine/docetaxel backbones) derive from glioma, meningioma or soft-tissue-sarcoma series and cannot be assumed to apply; (2) tolerability is the main therapeutic asset of the current regimen - the patient has had no significant toxicity, so the marginal benefit of adding a drug is unproven while the cost is predictable: cumulative temozolomide lymphopenia plus a myelosuppressive partner (platinum, etoposide, anthracycline) increases infection, transfusion and dose-delay risk, and may force dose reductions of the drug that is actually working; (3) escalation should be driven by objective progression on imaging or clinical deterioration, not by elapsed time or family anxiety - the rule agreed with the patient should be: if the residual grows on the next MRI or symptoms worsen, change class rather than simply stack a second agent onto TMZ; (4) the higher-yield use of the next weeks is diagnostic and local-control work that changes what the next drug will be: FFPE methylation profiling and DNA/RNA NGS on the 2026-10-19 biopsy and 2026-10-28 resection blocks, orthogonal confirmation of any plasma NGS call in tumour tissue, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis to exclude an occult extracranial primary, and re-discussion of re-resection or stereotactic radiosurgery for the growing residual; (5) genuinely useful additions later are selected, not empirical - for example bevacizumab for angiogenesis-driven progression, or a molecularly selected targeted agent (see q3) - and an anthracycline-based sarcoma regimen if the diagnosis resolves that way; (6) exceptions in which I would change therapy now rather than wait: unequivocal radiographic progression on TMZ, new neurologic deficit or unrelieved raised intracranial pressure, unexplained or symptomatic cytopenias, or patient preference after a shared discussion of the limited evidence.
q3: Decision: no - do not stop temozolomide and do not switch to targeted therapy on the basis of this plasma ctDNA report alone. Continue TMZ to the planned MRI reassessment, confirm the findings in tumour tissue, and let the confirmed molecular result plus the histologic work-up drive any change. Key reasons: (1) the histologic entity is still not established, and a molecular finding by itself neither defines a WHO CNS tumour entity nor creates a standard-of-care treatment indication - classification and therapy both still require tissue-based diagnosis, and the four alterations listed (FGFR2 fusion; KRAS, STK11, CTNNB1) are a mixture of potentially relevant and incidental findings, not a diagnosis; (2) analytic validity is not secure: this is plasma ctDNA with no matched normal and no tumour confirmation, KRAS is a recognised clonal-haematopoiesis-associated gene, and low-allele-fraction calls of any type can be CHIP or assay artefact - the FGFR2 fusion is the most tumour-relevant call and should be confirmed orthogonally on tumour (FISH, RNA-based sequencing or IHC surrogates on freshly cut scrolls from the archival blocks with pathologist-guided macro-dissection); the co-occurrence of an FGFR2 fusion with a KRAS alteration is itself atypical for a single FGFR2-driven clone (the two are usually mutually exclusive in FGFR2-rearranged carcinomas), which is further reason to test tumour before acting; (3) actionability is limited and tumour-specific: none of these is a tissue-agnostic target (unlike NTRK fusions, MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high disease, and the same panel should be checked or re-requested for TMB/MSI because a positive result would open a genuinely tumour-agnostic option); FGFR2 fusions are druggable with pemigatinib, futibatinib or erdafitinib, but those approvals are tumour-specific (principally intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, with some breast/endometrial and urothelial indications), so in this patient an FGFR inhibitor would be off-label or trial-based and would need both confirmation and a coherent diagnosis; KRAS has no established CNS-penetrant targeted option for this setting, STK11 is not itself a drug target (and loss is associated with an immune-excluded, checkpoint-poor-response microenvironment), and CTNNB1/Wnt activation has no approved inhibitor; (4) the FGFR2 fusion should broaden the differential rather than narrow the treatment plan: it raises the possibility of an FGFR2-rearranged mesenchymal neoplasm or of an occult extracranial malignancy - classically intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma - metastatic to the brain/meninges, so complete systemic staging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with liver protocol, FDG-PET if indicated) and, if an extracranial primary is found, biopsy it, which would also re-frame the whole case; (5) the safe sequence is: continue the tolerated TMZ now (the residual is growing and the patient needs active therapy), send tissue confirmation and FFPE methylation profiling, repeat neuraxis MRI at the planned checkpoint, and only if the fusion is confirmed in tumour discuss an FGFR inhibitor - in a trial if possible, or off-label with shared decision-making - either as a change of class on progression or, exceptionally, earlier if progression is rapid; (6) keep the local-control options alive in parallel: re-resection of the growing residual adjacent to eloquent cortex would provide both therapy and the tissue needed to confirm this molecular result.
